author: Claude
headline: Dow jumps nearly 600 points to close out its best week since 2022; chip dips bounce hard
summary: The Dow rallied nearly 600 points to close out its best week since 2022, with the S&P 500 ending the day about 1.6% higher. Chip stocks led the rebound: Micron rose 7.6%, Dell 6.7%, Arm 6.2%, Intel 5.4% and AMD 4.6%, though a CNBC piece notes Jensen Huang's return did little to ease AI jitters. The backdrop still reads Cautious. The dip picks are led by Cisco, ASML, Intel, AMD, TSMC, Dell and Micron, with UnitedHealth, Freeport-McMoRan, Rio Tinto, Nvidia and Arm also well below their highs. Because several have bounced this week, buying in smaller amounts spreads the risk if the dips continue. Not financial advice.
points: Dow rallied nearly 600 points to close out its best week since 2022.
Chip rebound: Micron +7.6%, Dell +6.7%, Arm +6.2%, Intel +5.4%, AMD +4.6%, TSMC +3.2%; Nvidia +0.8%.
OpenAI countersued Apple for stealing trade secrets; hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform.
Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy in Europe; SpaceX shares jumped over 4%.
Crypto: every coin is still falling. Intuit and Reckitt are flagged as falling knives; Coca-Cola, Marriott and AbbVie are on the wait-for-a-dip list.
